checks.observed: STRUCTURAL, NOT RE-MEASURED. Round 5 adds a doorstep derivation, a lamp clamp and two prop sign fixes. No map pin, no waypoint, no compass, no objective marker. Round 1 measured the census properly and nothing here adds one.

ar3.note: Two crossings, and this round makes the second one demonstrable at an entity rather than asserted. (1) Round 3's stands: a town's masonry becomes sim.cell and sim/stealth/system.js:223 reads sim.cell.shapes.length to decide whether cover exists at all. (2) The join sizes the rooms the interior lamp model lights, and the round-5 clamp puts those lamps back inside the rooms. I measured the crossing live: with the lamps where the derivation leaves them an enemy two metres away reaches alert 100 / AGGRO; with every lamp in the room moved 60 m the same enemy reaches 80 / SUSPICIOUS; restoring them returns it to 100 / AGGRO. A settlement-layout decision moves a Souls-side alert state, inside the fixed step, reversibly.

score.note: Round 1 3.2 (gate 6), round 2 4.4, round 3 4.6, round 4 4.7, now 4.8. RI-WLD13 rises 3 -> 5, the largest single-item move this piece has had since round 2, and it is deserved: the containment half of the door is genuinely fixed and genuinely measurable for the first time in five rounds, and I reproduced it with my own instrument offline and live. It does not carry the item further because min-over-axes finds the OTHER half of the same object worse than it was — 19 of 115 doorsteps cannot put you back in the room you left, against 7 before this round — and because 0-of-115 is a fact about frame 1 and the number at rest is 10.

status_reasons: The headline is TRUE and independently reproduced: 115 doors, 0 bodies inside a drawn building one frame after exitInterior(), with a control at 113. Offline, 0 of 113 declared doorsteps satisfy insideBuilding().
But the round measured the one frame at which its number is zero. The same 115 doors read at 30/120/600 fixed steps give 8/10/10 bodies indoors, stable from frame 120, in ten named rooms.

Re-entry regressed and the round's number for it is wrong in kind. Its rollup counts door_in_reach truthy (106); doorAt() returns the NEAREST door of the town, so pressing interact returns you to the room you left on 96 of 115, into a different building on 10, into nothing on 9 — against 108/5/2 with the derivation cut. Moving 112 doors onto entry walls put four pairs of Blackrose doors 1.00 m apart.

The prop count is published under a predicate the round's code does not implement: its words describe overhang, its code computes clearance. At 1fda355 the number is 61 meshes in 49 rooms under overhang (the round-4 verdict's predicate, at the same 0.6 m the verdict DID state) and 0 under clearance.

A second enumeration blind spot, inside the fix for the first: applyInteriorBounds()'s orphan pass does `if (!plan) continue` BEFORE its own counter, so barge-hold and writ-house — both declaring settlement 'tidewrack', which is not one of the eight settlement documents — are reached by no offline loop in this piece, including the fail-closed check the round shipped.
The lamp fix is real, confirmed by three instruments including the round-4 critic's own, and reaches an entity's behaviour.
what_the_round_got_right: The blocking gap it was given is CLOSED at the frame it measures, and I verified it with an instrument the builder did not write, offline and live.

The reason the door had to be written IN PLACE through the settlement document is correct and load-bearing: SettlementSystem's reach table is built in its constructor at engine.js:324, before setSettlements() ever runs, and each row holds the b.door array itself.

The 2x2 is honestly labelled and its shape is right — two INDEPENDENT fixes, not two guards for one defect and not an inert fix. I reproduced its two corner cells with my own arms and got byte agreement: doorstep cut 113, lamp clamp cut 153.

The teardowns bite. w1-04-r5-census.mjs --self-break calls buildInterior(rec) with the wrong arity on purpose and exits 1 with PROBE FAILURE on 115 of 115 rooms — the correct, armed answer to the exact failure the round-4 critic made and reported.
The lamp clamp is confirmed by a third instrument: the ROUND-4 CRITIC's own critic-w1-04-r4-offline.mjs, re-run at 1fda355, reports C3 = 0 lamps outside in 0 rooms against its own 55 at round 4.
The lamp fix is not a fork: sim/stealth/system.js is untouched, and lightSourceCensus() reads the same LightField object the fixed step samples. Verified by source, not taken.

The consumption aggregation was run, is green for the right reason, and row 10a's defect (comparing the previous door's town to this one's) is properly fixed by establishing the street AT the door under test.

The blind-spot finding the round made itself — three interiors naming a building no settlement document contains — is the best object in the round, and the census now says out loud that it used to be blind to them.
The stair_narrow / ladder_steep sign error (treads along local -z, backwards through the wall the slot leans on) is a real, well-diagnosed and well-fixed bug in 13 inns and halls.
It killed its own first live run BY PID rather than pkill'ing headless_shell, and said so.

biggest_gap.what: Pressing `interact` on the doorstep you were just put on — the real latch, sim/settlement.js#stepSettlement() reading input.pressedName('interact') and handing sim.door.interior to useDoor() — returns you to the room you left on 96 of 115 doors. On 10 it opens a DIFFERENT building (blackrose-house-0 -> blackrose-house-1 at 0.50 m, blackrose-inn -> blackrose-warders-hall 0.50, blackrose-market -> blackrose-smithy 0.50, blackrose-rootpost -> blackrose-clerk 0.50, lilmoth-customs -> lilmoth-yard 1.56, soulrest-boneyard -> soulrest-pawn 2.12, soulrest-court-steps -> soulrest-market 0.88, soulrest-grey-hist -> soulrest-court-steps 0.45, thorn-hall -> thorn-apothecary 0.16, thorn-house-0 -> thorn-gate 0.46). On 9 it opens nothing. Before this round moved the doors onto entry walls the same measurement was 108 / 5 / 2. The cause is that doorAt() returns the NEAREST door of the town within DOOR_REACH_M and there are now five pairs of doors within 2.6 m of each other, four of them exactly 1.00 m apart. Separately and by the same cause, 10 of 115 bodies are standing inside a drawn building 120 fixed steps after the door, having been clear of every footprint at frame 1.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: RI-WLD13 is interior/exterior continuity, and 'the door I came out of is the door I go back in by' is the other end of the object this round just fixed. A player meets it by turning round. It is also invisible to every instrument in five rounds of this piece, because they all measure a doorstep against BUILDINGS (insideBuilding, buildingAt) and none measures it against the DOOR TABLE.

other_gaps.what: w1-04-r5-census.mjs publishes '192 meshes in 28 rooms -> 0' under the definition 'a built mesh whose world bounding box REACHES more than 0.6 m outside its own room's bounds_m'. Its code computes `Math.max(bx[0] - box.max.x, box.min.x - bx[1], 0)` — how far the whole box sits CLEAR of the room, which is 0 whenever the box still overlaps the room at all, so a two-metre bench with 1.9 m through the wall scores zero. The round-4 verdict DID state its tolerance (0.6 m, §4(c)) and used the OVERHANG predicate. Measured both at 1fda355 with all of round 5's fixes in: OVERHANG 61 meshes in 49 rooms (all prop:hel_shell_roof, worst 0.95 m); CLEARANCE 0. The round-4 critic's own instrument re-run at 1fda355 independently gives 61 in 49. The fix itself is real either way — the 179 light fittings that dominated the round-4 count are gone to zero under BOTH predicates.

The status file says 'the door is back in reach from the doorstep on 106 of 115'. 10 of those 106 are a DIFFERENT building's door; the number that answers the question the sentence asks is 96.

self_audit.self_audit_note: MY OWN PROBE DEFECTS, REPORTED. (1) My first consumption-at-an-entity arm read enemy alert 0 / IDLE in every arm and I nearly published 'the lamp model does not reach an entity' as a finding about the build. It was my fixture: stepPerception() gates the sight channel on |bearing| > sight_cone_deg/2 and an enemy spawned with the default yaw faces away, so it fell through to hearing, and a still player makes no sound. Rule 4 caught it; the tool now aims the enemy and gives the player a motion band, and its header says why. (2) My first shot run reported all three captures failed; two had in fact succeeded and I was not copying the daemon's cache path to docs/shots/. (3) Two of those captures were then DELETED rather than published — one was empty sky under a name claiming an interior, one was near-black. NOT DONE, plainly: inCoverFraction on both arms (I established only where it reaches); the observed-theft branch; RI-WLD03 M13 (rule 25 bars me, fourth correct deferral, it needs its own dispatch); the inside of archon-market and a camera on the doorstep looking back (section 9); and I did not determine whether the ten settling bodies are a collision-solver defect or a doorstep-placement defect — I measured only that they settle indoors and stay there. My instrument's --self-break was watched go red on both arms and exits non-zero if either stays green.
